disclaimer: Indicative eligibility only. Criteria, amounts and deadlines change; always confirm on the official portal before applying.

schemes.name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi
schemes.benefit: ₹6,000 per year, paid in three instalments of ₹2,000 directly to your bank account.
schemes.description: Income support for landholding farmer families.
caveats: You must own cultivable land.
Income-tax payers and some government employees are excluded.
steps: Go to pmkisan.gov.in and open 'Farmers Corner' > 'New Farmer Registration'.
Enter Aadhaar number, mobile number and state, then fill in land and bank details.
Complete e-KYC (OTP or at a Common Service Centre).
Your state officer verifies the land record; track status under 'Know Your Status'.

schemes.name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
schemes.benefit: Insurance cover for crop loss from drought, flood, pests and other natural causes at a low farmer premium (about 2% for kharif and 1.5% for rabi food crops).
schemes.description: Protects farmers from financial loss when crops fail.
caveats: Enrol before the cut-off date for each crop season.
steps: Visit pmfby.gov.in or your bank, Common Service Centre or insurance agent before the season's cut-off date.
Choose your crop and area, and fill in the application with land details.
Pay the farmer share of the premium.
Report any crop loss within 72 hours through the Crop Insurance app or helpline 14447.

schemes.name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
schemes.benefit: Short-term farm credit at concessional interest, with interest subvention for timely repayment.
schemes.description: Easy, low-interest credit for seeds, fertiliser and other farming costs.
caveats: Borrowers over 60 may need a co-borrower.
steps: Visit your nearest bank branch or Common Service Centre, or apply on the bank's KCC page.
Submit the KCC form with ID, address and land documents.
The bank assesses your credit limit based on your crop and land.
Receive the card and use it for withdrawals and farm purchases.

schemes.name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Health Cover)
schemes.benefit: Free hospital treatment up to ₹5 lakh per family per year at empanelled hospitals. All citizens aged 70+ are covered regardless of income.
schemes.description: Cashless secondary and tertiary hospital care for poor and vulnerable families and for senior citizens.
caveats: For under-70s, eligibility is decided by SECC deprivation criteria and state lists, not income alone.
Check your name at the official 'Am I Eligible' page.
documents: Ration card or other family ID
steps: Check eligibility at mera.pmjay.gov.in using your mobile number or ration card.
Download the Ayushman App or visit a Common Service Centre or empanelled hospital's Ayushman Mitra desk.
Complete e-KYC with Aadhaar and get your Ayushman card (70+ seniors can apply for the Vay Vandana card).
Show the card for cashless treatment at any empanelled hospital.

schemes.name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Housing)
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs / Ministry of Rural Development
schemes.benefit: Financial assistance or an interest subsidy on home loans for building or buying a first pucca house.
schemes.description: Support for economically weaker, low-income and middle-income households to own a home.
caveats: Your family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India.
Income bands: EWS up to ₹3 lakh, LIG ₹3-6 lakh, MIG ₹6-9 lakh (urban, interest subsidy).
Rural households use PMAY-Gramin with its own list.
steps: Visit pmaymis.gov.in (urban) or pmayg.nic.in (rural) and select 'Apply for PMAY'.
Choose your category (EWS, LIG, MIG) and fill in family, income and Aadhaar details.
Submit the form, or apply via your Urban Local Body, Gram Panchayat or Common Service Centre.
Track your application status with the acknowledgement number.

schemes.name: PM Ujjwala Yojana (Free LPG Connection)
schemes.benefit: A deposit-free LPG connection for women from poor households, with a subsidy on refills.
schemes.description: Clean cooking fuel for women in low-income families.
caveats: The household must be poor (BPL, ration card or SECC criteria) and have no existing LPG connection.
steps: Download the KYC form from pmuy.gov.in or collect it from your local LPG distributor.
Fill in family details and attach ID and BPL proof.
Submit it to the nearest LPG distributor.
After verification, receive your connection and first cylinder.

schemes.name: Atal Pension Yojana (APY)
schemes.benefit: A guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 from age 60, depending on your monthly contribution.
schemes.description: A retirement savings scheme built for people in the unorganised sector.
caveats: Income-tax payers cannot join.
You need a savings bank account with auto-debit.
steps: Visit your bank or post office where you have a savings account.
Fill in the APY registration form with nominee details.
Choose the pension amount; the monthly contribution is set by your joining age.
Keep balance in your account for the auto-debit each month.

schemes.name: PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (Life Insurance)
schemes.benefit: ₹2 lakh life insurance cover for ₹436 a year, auto-debited from your bank account.
schemes.description: Low-cost term life cover for bank account holders.
caveats: Renewable each year until age 55.
Premium amounts can be revised; check with your bank.
steps: Visit your bank branch, or use net banking or mobile banking.
Fill in the PMJJBY form and give an auto-debit consent.
Name a nominee.
The premium is debited every year around 31 May.

schemes.name: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana (Accident Insurance)
schemes.benefit: ₹2 lakh for accidental death or full disability and ₹1 lakh for partial disability, for ₹20 a year.
schemes.description: Very low-cost accident insurance for bank account holders.
caveats: Renewable yearly; ₹20 premium may be revised.
steps: Visit your bank branch, or use net or mobile banking.
Submit the PMSBY enrolment form with auto-debit consent.
Add nominee details.
Premium is debited annually in May/June.

schemes.name: PM Jan Dhan Yojana (Zero-Balance Bank Account)
schemes.benefit: A zero-balance bank account with a RuPay debit card, built-in accident cover and overdraft facility.
schemes.description: Gets every adult into the banking system.
caveats: For people without any existing bank account (or who can convert an old account).
documents: Aadhaar card or other officially valid ID
steps: Visit any bank branch or Bank Mitra (Business Correspondent).
Fill the Jan Dhan account opening form and complete KYC.
Collect your RuPay debit card and passbook.
Link Aadhaar and mobile number to receive benefits directly.

schemes.name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendor Loan)
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free working-capital loans starting at ₹15,000, with higher limits on timely repayment, plus an interest subsidy and digital-payment cashback.
schemes.description: Credit for street vendors to restart and grow their business.
caveats: You need a Certificate of Vending or an ID/Letter of Recommendation from your Urban Local Body.
steps: Apply at pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in or visit a Common Service Centre or your Urban Local Body.
Enter your mobile number and submit vending details.
Your application is processed by a bank or lending institution.
Receive the loan and repay on time to unlock the next, larger loan.

schemes.name: PM MUDRA Yojana (Business Loan)
schemes.benefit: Collateral-free loans for small businesses: Shishu (up to ₹50,000), Kishor (up to ₹5 lakh), Tarun (up to ₹10 lakh) and Tarun Plus (up to ₹20 lakh).
schemes.description: Funding for non-farm small and micro enterprises.
caveats: The business must be non-farm (manufacturing, trading or services).
Tarun Plus is for those who have repaid earlier loans.
steps: Prepare a short business plan and gather ID and address documents.
Apply at any bank, NBFC or microfinance institution, or at udyamimitra.in.
Choose the Shishu, Kishor or Tarun category based on the amount you need.
Loan is sanctioned after verification; you receive a MUDRA card.

schemes.name: Stand-Up India (Entrepreneur Loan)
schemes.benefit: Bank loans of ₹10 lakh to ₹1 crore to set up a new enterprise.
schemes.description: Loans for women and SC/ST entrepreneurs starting a first-time venture.
caveats: For greenfield (new) enterprises in manufacturing, services, trading or agri-allied activities.
steps: Register at standupmitra.in and prepare a project report.
Apply online or through a bank branch, the Lead District Manager or SIDBI.
The bank evaluates the proposal and sanctions the loan.
Receive funds and start operations.

schemes.name: PM Vishwakarma (Artisans & Craftspeople)
schemes.benefit: Free skill training with a daily stipend, a ₹15,000 toolkit incentive, and collateral-free loans of ₹1 lakh then ₹2 lakh at a concessional 5% interest.
schemes.description: Support for traditional artisans such as carpenters, potters, tailors, blacksmiths and cobblers.
caveats: You must work in one of the 18 listed traditional trades.
Only one member per family can register.
steps: Register at pmvishwakarma.gov.in through a Common Service Centre.
Complete biometric e-KYC.
Your Gram Panchayat or Urban Local Body and the district committee verify your application.
Receive a PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID card, then access training, toolkit and loans.

schemes.name: National Scholarship Portal Schemes
schemes.ministry: Ministry of Education and other ministries
schemes.benefit: Scholarships covering fees and maintenance allowance for students from low-income families, including SC, ST, OBC and minority categories.
schemes.description: One portal for central and state scholarships.
caveats: The income limit differs by scholarship (often ₹1 lakh to ₹4.5 lakh).
Marks, course and category conditions apply.
steps: Register on scholarships.gov.in (One Time Registration) and note your OTR ID.
Log in, choose the scholarships you qualify for, and fill in the application.
Upload your documents and submit before the deadline.
Your institute and nodal officer verify the form; money is credited to your bank account.

schemes.name: Skill India / PMKVY (Free Skill Training)
schemes.benefit: Free short-term skill training with a certificate and placement support in hundreds of job roles.
schemes.description: Industry-relevant training for students, dropouts and unemployed youth.
caveats: Course availability depends on your district's training centres and current scheme phase.
steps: Create a profile on skillindiadigital.gov.in.
Search for a course and training centre near you.
Enrol and complete the training and assessment.
Receive a certificate and attend placement support.

schemes.name: e-Shram Card (Unorganised Workers)
schemes.benefit: A national registration ID for unorganised workers with ₹2 lakh accidental insurance cover and access to other welfare schemes.
schemes.description: A database and benefits gateway for gig, domestic, construction and other informal workers.
caveats: You must not be an EPFO/ESIC member or an income-tax payer.
steps: Visit eshram.gov.in and click 'Register on e-Shram'.
Enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number and complete OTP verification.
Fill in occupation, education and bank details.
Download your UAN card; you can also register at a Common Service Centre.

schemes.name: PM Shram Yogi Maandhan (Pension for Workers)
schemes.benefit: A guaranteed monthly pension of ₹3,000 after age 60, with a small monthly contribution matched by the government.
schemes.description: Old-age security for informal-sector workers with low income.
caveats: Monthly income must be ₹15,000 or less.
You must not be a member of EPFO, ESIC or NPS.
documents: Savings bank account or Jan Dhan account
steps: Visit your nearest Common Service Centre with your Aadhaar and bank passbook.
Self-certify your income and complete Aadhaar-based registration.
Pay the first contribution in cash; you receive a Shram Yogi pension account number.
Contributions are auto-debited from your bank account each month.

schemes.name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension (NSAP)
schemes.benefit: A monthly old-age pension for poor senior citizens. The central share starts at ₹200 (₹500 at 80+); state governments add to it.
schemes.description: Basic income support for elderly people below the poverty line.
caveats: You must belong to a BPL household.
Pension amount varies by state.
steps: Collect the application form from your Gram Panchayat, block office or municipal office (or your state's social-justice portal).
Attach age, BPL and identity proofs.
Submit to the local authority; it is verified at block or district level.
Once sanctioned, the pension is credited monthly to your bank account.
